chunks: As for what was narrated by al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Faḍālah, from Ḥusayn ibn ʿUthmān, from Samāʿah, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who slept through the morning prayer until the sun rose. He said: “He should perform the two rakʿahs, then perform the morning prayer.”

key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ: the two rakʿahs, referring to the two-unit prayer to be performed first
key_terms.الْغَدَاةِ: the morning prayer, referring here to salat al-fajr
key_terms.طَلَعَتِ الشَّمْسُ: the sun rose, marking that the prayer time had passed
key_terms.نَامَ: slept, meaning the prayer was missed due to sleep

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he sleeps through salat al-ghadāh until after sunrise?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding one who misses salat al-ghadāh due to sleep until after sunrise. It states that he should first perform the two rakʿahs and then perform the morning prayer, indicating the order of making up these prayers.
